original_question: Consider the two-parameter family of Poisson brackets on R^3 defined by {f,g}_{a,ρ}(x,y,z)=ρ(x,y,z)·det(∂(a,f,g)/∂(x,y,z)), where a is a smooth function and ρ is a density in the chosen coordinates. Is this class preserved by any Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ=Q(P), and for a given symmetry does there exist an induced evolutionary system ȧ=A([a],[ρ]), ρ̇=R([a],[ρ]) whose pushforward under τ:(a,ρ)↦{·,·}_{a,ρ} equals Q(P([a],ρ))?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the paper’s Section 1 problem about whether Kontsevich graph-flow infinitesimal symmetries restrict to the Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets on affine R^3, formulated in Conjecture 1.1 and sharpened by the neighboring Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 via induced evolution of the Casimir a and the coordinate density/inverse-density parameter ρ.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core geometric object from the paper: the Nambu-determinant Poisson bracket on R^3 written in coordinates via a function a and a density factor ρ, together with the paper’s main restriction question: whether a Kontsevich infinitesimal Poisson symmetry Q(P) stays inside that class and can be represented by induced evolution equations for the underlying data (a,ρ). The use of the pushforward map τ:(a,ρ)↦P is also faithful to the paper’s intent.
missing_details: The paper treats a as a global Casimir and ρ as the coordinate density/inverse-density datum attached to the chosen affine coordinates on R^3; that role should be stated explicitly.
The ambient function class should be made explicit: smooth real-valued functions on affine R^3 with coordinates (x,y,z).
Q(P) is not an arbitrary infinitesimal deformation; it is a Kontsevich universal differential-polynomial Poisson 2-cocycle coming from a graph cocycle. That source of Q should be named.
The paper’s notion of 'preserved' is first-order/infinitesimal: one asks for an induced evolution whose linearization under τ reproduces Q(P).
The right-hand sides A([a],[ρ]) and R([a],[ρ]) are evolutionary differential-polynomial expressions in the jet variables of a and ρ, not arbitrary functionals.
The quantifiers should be stated carefully: for a fixed Kontsevich flow/symmetry Q, does the restriction exist for every admissible pair (a,ρ)?
The map τ should be identified as sending the parameter pair (a,ρ) to the corresponding Poisson bivector/bracket, and 'pushforward' should mean the Fréchet derivative Dτ_(a,ρ)(A,R).
The question should stay at the level of restriction of the infinitesimal flow, not broaden to full nonlinear time integration or to arbitrary Poisson brackets beyond the Nambu-determinant ansatz.
The distinction between the bracket formula and the equivalent Poisson bivector formulation should be made explicit so the question is fully stand-alone.
No extra generalization to arbitrary dimensions or arbitrary Kontsevich flows beyond the fixed flow under discussion should be added unless stated as such in the paper’s nearby formulation.
refined_question:
Let P(a,ρ) be the Nambu-determinant Poisson structure on the affine space R^3 with coordinates (x,y,z), defined by
{f,g}_{a,ρ}(x,y,z)=ρ(x,y,z)·det(∂(a,f,g)/∂(x,y,z)),
where a,ρ∈C^∞(R^3;R), so that a is a global Casimir of P(a,ρ). Fix a Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry of Poisson bivectors, i.e. a universal differential-polynomial Poisson 2-cocycle Q(P) arising from a graph cocycle. Does this flow restrict to the Nambu-determinant class in the following precise sense: for every pair (a,ρ), do there exist evolutionary differential-polynomial right-hand sides A([a],[ρ]) and R([a],[ρ]) such that, with τ(a,ρ)=P(a,ρ), one has Dτ_(a,ρ)(A,R)=Q(P(a,ρ))? Equivalently, can the first-order deformation Ṗ=Q(P) of the Poisson structure be realized entirely as an induced first-order evolution ȧ=A([a],[ρ]), ρ̇=R([a],[ρ]) within the same Nambu-determinant ansatz?
justification: The nearest paper-faithful target is not a broad question about arbitrary Poisson brackets, but the specific Section 1 restriction problem for the Nambu-determinant class on R^3. Your draft is already close because it uses the correct determinant bracket and asks exactly for preservation under a Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry together with induced evolution of the underlying parameters. What needed sharpening was the paper’s precise meaning of preservation: not mere invariance of form, but existence of differential-polynomial evolutionary laws for the Casimir and density data whose first-order pushforward under the parameterization map reproduces the Kontsevich graph-flow cocycle. That is why Conjecture 1.1 is the right target, while Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 supply the nearby precision/evidence that make the question stand alone in the paper’s own terms.
